threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep looking up at the street signs for inspiration, forgetting every shop's got a different name than it had last week.
Caught a bloke singing old David Bowie on the 3 last night. Had the whole back of the bus clapping, proper Brixton vibe! Made the dreary ride feel like a gig.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a kebab shop serving midnight breakfast burritos. Only in Neukölln do cravings meet creativity like that.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you stumble upon a döner with a side of art installation in a public park—just another casual day in the Spree-side culture.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're from here when they can spot a tourist in Dolores Park just by their overly careful picnic setup.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy on a Muni bus argue with the driver about whether the next stop was Potrero or Mission. You'd think he was debating world peace.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Plaza del Sol is always lively, but it empties out by 11 PM. Locals prefer the secret corners after dark.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by the way they stand waiting for the light to change at pedestrian crossings—even at 3am.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it coffee; locals swear by ‘specialty brew’ like it’s a religion. Mind your words near the café on Kingsland Road.
Heard a woman singing 'Back to Black' on the 196 last night, and the whole bus joined in. Only in Brixton, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard a Turkish grandma bargaining for flowers at the market while juggling two kids and a bag of groceries—classic Neukölln hustle.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find spontaneous open-air raves next to busy S-Bahn stations. The bass drops, and commuters just shrug and dance.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: The way someone talks about dodging potholes on 16th feels uniquely San Francisco—like it’s a rite of passage, not just commuter frustration.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a musician bring the 49 bus to a standstill with a sax solo that turned rush hour into a moment of applause. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real heartbeat is in the hidden plazas where families gather, not the tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they’re still fascinated by the buskers on Carrer de Verdi, snapping photos like it's a tourist trap.
